relevance_note: Case report of an infant with a de novo TNFAIP3 frameshift variant: 'whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous variant in TNFAIP3'.
method_note: Read the whole paper and built the JSON with a short Python script in my scratch directory; every value was typed from my reading, and the script only checks that each span occurs verbatim (spans crossing thin spaces, e.g. around the degree signs and in the genomic coordinates, were cut from the paper text by start/end anchors). Single-patient case report; Table 1 is a laboratory table for that one patient (not patients as rows or columns). Its legend says 'The bold values provided in Table 1 indicates abnormal results', so bold lab values were recorded as observed abnormalities with that legend as a second span. The legend does not define '(-)', so no '(-)' cell was used to exclude anything (rule 6). Scope: both parents are included as tested-negative relatives ('neither parent carried the variant'); they get no variant rows and all checklist items are not reported. The two half-brothers ('had no similar medical history') were neither tested nor affected, so they get no rows. Two previously published people from the Discussion are included under v4 because individual-level facts are given: Iwasa (12) (33-year-old woman; elevated liver enzymes, jaundice, autoimmune hepatitis) and Zhang (7) (liver injury; positive CMV testing; onset in the neonatal period, where the sentence leaves unclear whether 'onset' refers to the case or the liver injury). No variant rows for them: the body text ties no TNFAIP3 variant to either person (reference-list titles were not used as evidence, e.g. ref 7's 'large deletion on chromosome 6q' and ref 6's 'a girl'). Zhou (1) and the other cited references are group-level only. Genital ulcers were marked excluded from the admission examination ('No abnormalities were detected in the anus or external genitalia'), a broad absence covering ulcers. Not marked: cytopenia (autoimmune), although haemoglobin is low and the direct antiglobulin test positive (the paper does not call it autoimmune cytopenia or haemolysis); recurrent infections, although COVID-19, enterovirus and Enterobacter cloacae (sputum) are reported (the paper does not describe recurrent infections); gastrointestinal inflammation (diarrhoea only; endoscopy declined); lymphoproliferation (spleen palpable 1.5 cm, not called splenomegaly). The admission age (48 days) is not an age at diagnosis; the diagnosis came during the readmission, with no age stated. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper says nothing either way. Discordances noted, not treated as feature contradictions: dsDNA positive by ELISA but '(-)' by IIF; MPO and PR3 antibodies positive while pANCA and cANCA are '(-)'. Possible typos in Table 1: creatinine printed with the same value and range as blood urea nitrogen ('3.03 mmol/L (0.8–5.3 mmol/L)'), and the red blood cell reference range repeats the white-cell range. The keyword 'newborn lupus' was not used as a diagnosis.
